Safe = the holder is provably dead (same host: pid gone; or lease expired beyond ttl+grace with no event, heartbeat or file change since) AND the tree is measured. Operator question 2026-10-18: should ddflow automate the stale checks? Yes. Seen all day: agents report 'waiting on the review/ci/pins' for 15 to 60 minutes after the background process they started died, was killed, or finished and its monitor was lost (fleet-dx-l, fleet-bugs2, fleet-unblock-b). DX-health-watch detects idle, stalled, unresponsive, locked, crashed and runaway lanes, but it cannot tell a LEGITIMATE long wait (a DeepSeek review of 15-30 minutes) from a DEAD one, so it either nudges the legitimate waits or misses the dead ones. Needs one fact: the live-run registry (services/gates/running.py, shared with DX-gate-run-same-commit-live, DX-review-concurrent-runs and DX-gate-run-detach): every gate/review/ci/pins run records item, gate, pid, start time, log path and expected duration; the finish records the outcome. New finding ORPHAN_WAIT: a lane with no progress for [health].orphan_s (default 300) whose newest registry entry is finished or whose pid is gone with no recorded outcome: 'DX-x waits on review rubber_duck: run 4412 ended 12 min ago (outcome recorded: passed, see ddflow gate status) / died with no outcome (log: ...); rerun: ddflow review DX-x --gate rubber_duck'. The opposite check: a lane whose registered run is alive and within its expected duration is NOT idle or stalled (no nudge). The correction ladder is the existing one (nudge, then stop request); the nudge text and the heartbeat reply carry the finding so the agent itself sees it. Also exposed in ddflow lanes and ddflow health.

Folded B-res-inflight-gates (A gate or review killed mid-run is visible and resumable: dangling gate.started, stray child processes, partial review rounds): D-recovery-one-design (operator 2026-10-23: D-orphan-recovery governs; fold the four overlapping pairs).

A gate.started with no outcome and no live process is shown by gate status as 'interrupted at <time>, re-run' (not just pending); gate and reviewer subprocesses run in their own process group and are killed when their lease lapses or ddflow dies; each review chunk's result is persisted as it arrives so a re-run reviews only the missing chunks (the --chunk machinery exists); the round is counted only when it finishes. roborev async jobs are tracked by job id so a restart waits for the job instead of enqueuing another (absorbs B-roborev-wait-by-job).
